feed.title: The SpaceX Dispatch
feed.subtitle: Weekday briefing on SpaceX launches, Starlink, AI and the SPCX stock
feed.rights: The SpaceX Dispatch is an independent weekday digest of public news, X posts, regulatory filings and market data about Space Exploration Technologies Corp., and is not affiliated with the company. Quotes are verbatim; emoji in quoted posts are omitted for print. Market data are delayed and may be revised. Not investment advice.

entry.title: Friday, October 23, 2026: A 9.1% drop as the first lock-up opens
entry.summary:
SPCX fell 9.14% to $144.75 on Thursday, on 195 million shares, about twice its 30-session average, giving back all of Wednesday's 7.79% gain and more. The slide "followed profit-taking and a share unlock," The Motley Fool wrote; under the prospectus, up to 1.3 billion locked-up Class A shares could be sold from Thursday, with up to 328.4 million more from Saturday. The Nasdaq 100 lost 2.90% and the S&P 500 1.21%.

After the close, SpaceX filed its third-quarter 10-Q, which puts the Tesla talks in writing: "our board of directors has formed a special committee to evaluate a potential combination between SpaceX and Tesla, Inc.," and "No determination by our special committee has been made." Starlink 15-15, scrubbed a third straight day on Thursday, tries again this evening.

entry.title: Thursday, October 22, 2026: A 7.8% jump, and a lock-up opens
entry.summary:
SPCX closed up 7.79% at $159.31 on Wednesday, on 219 million shares, more than twice its 30-session average, after SpaceX "posted its first profit as a public company," Reuters reported. Analysts lifted price targets across the board; JPMorgan's Doug Anmuth more than doubled his to $500, writing that "SpaceX's ambitions are bigger than any company's we've seen," CNBC reported.

From Thursday, up to 1.3 billion locked-up Class A shares, 28% of those under the 180-day lock-up, can be sold, followed by up to 328.4 million on Saturday and the rest on December 8, under the prospectus. A Starlink launch from California was scrubbed for weather Wednesday evening and tries again tonight.

entry.title: Wednesday, October 21, 2026: Revenue up 161% as AI becomes the biggest business
entry.summary:
SpaceX reported third-quarter revenue of $14.58 billion, against the $12.72 billion analysts expected, and net income of $4.4 billion, compared with a $1.1 billion loss a year earlier, Reuters reported. The Super Intelligence (SI) segment brought in $7.6 billion, more than Starlink and launch combined, according to the company's results release.

"We are in an inflection moment for SpaceX across launch, connectivity and superintelligence," Musk said on the call. SPCX, which closed down 0.11% at $147.79 on Tuesday, rose 4.6% after hours, Bloomberg Law reported. That evening, a Starlink launch from California was scrubbed for a technical issue.

entry.title: Tuesday, October 20, 2026: Starfall flies again on results day
entry.summary:
A Falcon 9 lifted off from Cape Canaveral at 7:04 a.m. EDT Tuesday with Bandwagon-5, a rideshare of 32 payloads that includes the second flight of SpaceX's Starfall return capsule, a day late because of recovery weather. The booster landed on the drone ship A Shortfall of Gravitas, and payload deployments began about an hour after launch (SpaceX).

After the close, SpaceX reports its third quarter, its second report as a public company. Musk's pledged share for every American child will go through Trump Accounts, President Trump said Monday, The Verge reported. SPCX rose 1.32% to $147.96 on Monday.

entry.title: Monday, October 19, 2026: Results tomorrow, and a share for every child
entry.summary:
SpaceX reports its third quarter after the close on Tuesday, its second report as a public company, and up to 1.3 billion locked-up shares become sellable two trading days later. "Next year, I will give one of my SpaceX shares to every kid in America. This will be the first of many," Elon Musk posted at 3:52 a.m. EDT Monday, a gift worth about $10.5 billion at Friday's close, CNBC calculated.

Bandwagon-5 slipped a day to Tuesday because of recovery weather. New York City Council members called SpaceXAI's testimony on Grok safety evasive, and Ukraine's president blamed Washington for Starshield speed limits. SPCX fell 1.74% to $146.03 on Friday.

entry.title: Friday, October 16, 2026: USSF-481 flies, Dragon docks, and SpaceX lends Tesla its thrusters
entry.summary:
A Falcon 9 launched the classified USSF-481 mission from Vandenberg at 8:01 p.m. EDT Thursday, 17 minutes into its window, and the booster landed on its 28th flight, Spaceflight Now reported. An hour later, at a SpaceX test site in McGregor, Texas, Tesla's new Roadster flew on SpaceX cold-gas thrusters. "Tesla x SpaceX," Elon Musk posted.

Cargo Dragon docked at the space station Thursday morning. Ukraine says its Starlink and Starshield service is back to full capacity. Musk says the Star Mind orbital computer SpaceX is building with Nvidia reaches volume production next year, and SpaceXAI testifies to the New York City Council at 10 a.m. EDT today. SPCX fell 2.33% to $148.62.

entry.title: Thursday, October 15, 2026: A Starshield speed limit hits Ukraine's front line; Musk says Washington decides
entry.summary:
Ukrainian officials said military Starshield terminals were restricted while moving overnight into Wednesday, slowing drones and ground robots. "Starshield systems are owned and controlled by the US government. Any limits on speed or usage are decided by the US military and ultimately POTUS," Elon Musk replied to Ukraine's Mykhailo Fedorov, who had said connectivity at up to 160 km/h was being restored.

Cargo Dragon is due to dock at the International Space Station (ISS) at about 11 a.m. EDT today, and a Falcon 9 is scheduled to launch the USSF-481 mission from California at 7:44 p.m. EDT. SPCX fell 2.80% to $152.16 as a hot inflation report hit AI-linked stocks. There were no new SEC filings.

entry.title: Wednesday, October 14, 2026: FAA opens a full environmental review of 456 Starship launches a year from Starbase
entry.summary:
The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) published a notice today that it will prepare a programmatic environmental impact statement on SpaceX's plan to raise Starship operations at Starbase, Texas, to as many as 456 launches and 912 landings a year, from 25 launches today. Public scoping meetings are set for November 17 to 19, with comments due November 30. SPCX fell 4.21% to $156.54 on Tuesday, the day the plan became public.

Ship 40, the first Starship to come back to its launch site after flying, now stands in a Megabay, where SpaceX says it will yield "first-of-its-kind data" on a flown heatshield. Cargo Dragon is due at the space station Thursday, the same evening a Falcon 9 is scheduled to launch USSF-481. SpaceXAI agreed to testify before the New York City Council on Friday. There were no new SEC filings.

entry.title: Tuesday, October 13, 2026: Two Falcon 9s in ten hours: Starlink from California, then cargo Dragon to the station
entry.summary:
Falcon 9 launched 27 Starlink satellites from Vandenberg at 8:28 p.m. EDT Monday, the first Falcon 9 Starlink mission since September 19, and then sent NASA's 35th cargo Dragon (CRS-35) toward the International Space Station (ISS) from Cape Canaveral at 6:33 a.m. EDT today. Dragon is due to dock on Thursday at about 11 a.m. EDT; its booster landed at Landing Zone 40. A Bandwagon-5 rideshare is now dated for Monday, October 19.

SpaceX's AI arm unified Grok, Cursor and X Premium into one five-tier plan, The X Subscription. Poland said two Turkish citizens were arrested in Germany over a fire at a Starlink ground station that Warsaw blames on Russian intelligence. India's communications ministry called complaints about Starlink's wait "baseless." SPCX rose 0.52% to $163.42. There were no new SEC or FAA filings.

entry.title: Monday, October 12, 2026: The SDA satellites fly, and Musk puts a ship catch on Starship's next flight
entry.summary:
A Falcon 9 finally launched 21 Space Development Agency (SDA) data-relay satellites from California early Saturday, five days after an automatic abort, and its booster landed back at Vandenberg. Two more Falcon 9s are lined up: Starlink 15-25 on Monday evening, after slipping from Saturday and Sunday, and the CRS-35 cargo Dragon to the International Space Station (ISS) at 6:33 a.m. EDT Tuesday.

Speaking by video at a Tesla fan event in Texas on Saturday, Elon Musk said Starship Flight 15, "hopefully" four to six weeks away, will try to catch the ship with the launch tower. Starlink won a full operating license in Venezuela and offered free service in quake-hit Panama, while Musk escalated his fight with Mukesh Ambani over India. SPCX rose 1.25% Friday to $162.57 as Barclays started coverage at Overweight. SpaceX has filed nothing new with the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) since Friday morning.

entry.title: Friday, October 9, 2026: SpaceX buys its way into the phone business, and carrier stocks take the hit
entry.summary:
After the market closed on Thursday, SpaceX said it will buy Grain Management's nationwide 800 MHz spectrum portfolio, up to 14 megahertz of paired low-band airwaves that it says will let Starlink Mobile "become a major mobile carrier in the US." The price was not disclosed; The Wall Street Journal reported about $8 billion in cash. The deal still needs approval from the Federal Communications Commission (FCC). By Friday morning, shares of AT&T, Verizon and T-Mobile were down 5.5% to 7.4% before the open, Reuters reported.

The news came too late to help SPCX, which fell 4.19% to $160.57 during Thursday's session, its second straight loss, before rising about 2.5% in extended trading. Up to 328.4 million more Class A shares become free to sell from Friday under the IPO lock-up schedule. Crew-12 is home after Thursday's splashdown. Next on the launch schedule: a Space Development Agency (SDA) mission early Saturday and the CRS-35 cargo flight on Tuesday. SpaceX has filed nothing new with the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) since Thursday morning.

entry.title: Thursday, October 8, 2026: Crew-12 splashes down, Starlink signs up whole airlines, and Elon Musk takes his India fight public
entry.summary:
The Dragon capsule Freedom splashed down off Los Angeles at 11:34 a.m. EDT Thursday, bringing four Crew-12 astronauts home after 237 days at the International Space Station (ISS). Starlink had a strong day with airlines: American Airlines will put it on its entire mainline fleet of more than 1,000 jets, KLM will offer it free on long-haul flights from mid-2027, and Royal Air Maroc became the first African airline to sign on.

In India, Elon Musk accused "certain oligarchs" of blocking Starlink's license, and the government called the claim baseless. On Wall Street, a report that SpaceX is seeking about $40 billion of debt to buy Nvidia chips helped push SPCX down 2.51% to $167.60 on Wednesday, ending a three-day run. In Washington, the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) put two direct-to-device spectrum proposals on its October 29 agenda. SpaceX has filed nothing new with the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) since Wednesday morning.
